verdict.rationale: Stripe's agentic-commerce surface is deeply API/CLI-first: catalog import API, checkout session APIs with agent attribution, SPT issuance/revocation, MCP server exposing Stripe API tools, Link CLI for wallet/payment credentials, RAKs, and sandbox CLI provisioning all let an AI agent perform nearly every seller/buyer action programmatically, and Dashboard views (transactions tagged by agent) appear to be read/reporting layers over these same API objects. However, some steps are explicitly gated to human/Dashboard-only flows (e.g., MCP write-action approval requires clicking a Dashboard approval URL, seller onboarding/agent-terms review, OCA confirmation) rather than being fully API-drivable, so full UI/API parity isn't demonstrated. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or evidence that every Dashboard configuration/onboarding action has an API equivalent, and confirmation that human-approval gates aren't hard UI-only requirements.
